messages:
Ashley: Heads up — p95 on /api/v1/generate jumped ~30% at 11:07, but p50/p99 look steady. Dashboard shows the spike only for the "mobile" client cohort. Anyone else seeing weird provenance?
Jon: Hmm, I see the graph. Is that the new routing policy rollout from last night? @Maya any rollout weights changed?
Maya: No weight change on the rollout. I did push a small quota tweak: reduced burst quota for the mobile pool. Could that cause a latency artifact?
Ashley: Possibly. The spike aligns with a quota refill window. But why would p95 jump for mobile and not backend clients? Sampling or aggregation bug?
Priya: Can you paste the query you used to build the dashboard? might be an aggregation mismatch.
Ashley: Sure — this is the dashboard rollup query we're using (console):
```
SELECT pct(95, latency_ms) as p95, cnt
FROM requests
WHERE endpoint = '/api/v1/generate' AND cohort = 'mobile'
GROUP BY 1m
```
Jon: Two quick nits: 1) `group by 1m` uses our sampled ingestion which can bias percentiles when sample rate changes mid-window. 2) Are you mixing route tags vs endpoint aliases? we switched aliasing last week.
Maya: Good call on aliasing. We added `route_alias=mobile-v2` for some mobile traffic during a canary. The dashboard filter still uses `cohort='mobile'` which doesn't match alias. Could cause split counts.
Ashley: Interesting — split counts would explain p95 going up if lower tail traffic got sampled differently. The window had 40% fewer samples for the mobile cohort during the spike.
deploybot: deploybot: Can confirm a canary rolled at 2025-12-01T10:50:22Z -> route_alias `mobile-v2` created on gw-prod-3.
Priya: If sample counts differ across windows, tdigest-based pct() needs weight normalization. Our console pct() assumes uniform sampling.
Jon: Proposed quick triage:
- verify sample_rate by (samples_in_window / requests_in_window)
- recompute pct with raw histograms if available
- check KV cache hit rate and retry counts for mobile
Maya: I'll grep traces for retries. Also checking quota throttle logs for mobile pool.
Ashley: I recomputed raw histogram for the time slice and got p95 ~ stable (no 30% bump). When I compute pct() over sampled stream I see the bump.
Priya: So root cause = sampling-rate drift + alias split + dashboard query using sampled stream without weight correction.
Jon: Can we fix fast? Options:
- update dashboard to use raw histograms (if retention allows) — safest
- apply weight correction in pct() function — requires backend change
- fallback: add annotation to dashboard explaining sampling caveat
Maya: For immediate fix I'll switch the cohort filter to include `route_alias` variations so the sample counts rejoin. Long term we should prefer histograms for percentiles.
Ashley: Sounds good. @Operations can we add a monitor for sample_rate drops by cohort? Want automated alert if sample rate changes >20% vs baseline.
Operations: Ack. I'll add a monitor: `sample_rate_pct_change > 20%` for any cohort with endpoint `/api/v1/generate`.
Jon: Action items captured:
- Maya: update dashboard filters (include route_alias) — in 15m
- Operations: add sample-rate monitor — in 30m
- Priya/Infra: design pct() weighting / histogram fallback — RFC next week
Ashley: Thx all. I'll patch the dashboard and post before/after screenshots.
Maya: Patch live, filter now `cohort='mobile' OR route_alias LIKE 'mobile%'` :thumbsup:
Ashley: After patch, sample counts normalized and p95 back to baseline. Closing as root-cause = split alias + sampling bias.
Jon: We should add a short console doc blurb about when to use histograms vs sampled pct() — I'll draft.
Priya: I'll own the RFC for weight-corrected pct() implementation.
Ashley: Closing thread. Thanks everyone :partyparrot:
